ports.note: Takes the chosen product, and optionally a study area whose extent is searched; with no area connected, the extent is four edges typed in the dialog. Emits satellite-files: remote files not yet read, its own port type so nothing mistakes addresses for data.

ontology.note: The receipt states the catalog, collection, product, extent and where it came from (a study area or a typed extent), dates, how many items were returned, matched and kept, whether the search stopped at its limit, and fw:completenessRead false: a search reads no pixels. Held by fw:SatelliteCatalogSearchShape.

changes.description: The area port is optional. With no Study area connected, the dialog takes four typed edges, west, south, east and north, checked as typed (all four numbers; longitudes within ±180 and latitudes within ±90; west less than east, south less than north) and drawn before the search, after JLT's W/S/E/N field. The practitioner on 0.28.0, whose Search stayed grey without a Study area: "the search catalog UI is not enough for the search". The receipt states fw:searchAreaFrom. Saved 0.1.0 searches run unchanged and read as from a study area.

evidence.note: The search builder, its messages and the 500-item bound are JLT's, ported. Unit tests use a stubbed catalog; a live search was run against Planetary Computer in a browser. Nothing here reads a file, so nothing establishes that an item holds usable pixels over the area.
